output.lesson:
📚 The T-Rex had teeth as long as your entire hand!

Imagine holding a banana in your hand. Now imagine a tooth that size — sharp, serrated like a steak knife, and ready to crunch through bone. That's what T-Rex had in its mouth — sixty of them!

T-Rex lived about 66 million years ago, during a time called the Cretaceous period. It was one of the last dinosaurs to exist before a giant asteroid struck Earth and changed everything. The asteroid was so big that it created a crater 93 miles wide — that's like driving from San Francisco to San Jose and back!

But let's get back to T-Rex. It stood about 12 feet tall at the hips — that's taller than most grown-ups! And from its nose to the tip of its tail, it stretched 40 feet long. That's the length of a school bus. Imagine a school bus with teeth, running around at 12 miles per hour. That's faster than you can ride your bike!

T-Rex had tiny arms — only about three feet long. Scientists used to think these arms were useless, but now they believe T-Rex might have used them to hold onto prey while biting down. Even small arms can be strong when they belong to a 9-ton predator!

The name Tyrannosaurus Rex means Tyrant Lizard King in Greek. Tyranno means tyrant, saurus means lizard, and rex means king. So T-Rex was literally the king of the tyrant lizards!

Here's something amazing: T-Rex had the strongest bite of any land animal that ever lived. Its bite force was about 12,800 pounds — that's like having three small cars sitting on whatever it was biting down on. Crunch!

Scientists know all this because they study fossils. Fossils are the preserved remains of ancient animals. When T-Rex died, sometimes its bones got buried in mud and sand. Over millions of years, minerals seeped into the bones and turned them to stone. Paleontologists — scientists who study dinosaurs — dig up these fossils and put them together like giant puzzles.

The most complete T-Rex skeleton ever found is named Sue. Sue is 90% complete, which is incredibly rare. Most dinosaur skeletons are only 50-60% complete. Sue lives at the Field Museum in Chicago, and over 10 million people have visited to see her!

Did you know? T-Rex might have had feathers when it was young! Scientists have found fossils of other T-Rex relatives with feathery impressions around their bodies. Imagine a fuzzy baby T-Rex — cute but still deadly!

Ask your parents: If you could have any dinosaur as a pet (and it would be friendly), which one would you choose and why?
